summary.text: Trilobites are extinct marine arthropods, the class Trilobita, whose name means "three-lobed entities".
They lived in the oceans for almost 270 million years, and more than 22,000 species have been described.
Their calcite exoskeletons fossilized easily, leaving a large fossil record that has aided fields from evolutionary biology to plate tectonics.

items.prompt: Trilobites and their close artiopod relatives looked alike, yet trilobite fossils are far more common. Why?

options.label: Only trilobites had heavily mineralized exoskeletons
Only trilobites lived in shallow, muddy coastal water
Trilobites were much larger than all their relatives
Trilobites lived for centuries, so more bodies piled up

items.explain: Trilobites had hard calcite exoskeletons that fossilize easily, while other artiopods were largely unmineralized and turn up mainly in exceptional deposits.

items.prompt: How did trilobites as a group get their food?

options.label: Only by filtering food from the seabed
Only by hunting other small animals
In many ways, from hunting to eating plankton
Only by living as parasites on fish

items.explain: Trilobites filled many niches: some were predators, scavengers or filter feeders on the seabed, and some swam and ate plankton.

items.prompt: Some trilobites from Morocco still show their soft tissues. What most likely preserved them so well?

options.label: They were frozen solid in polar sea ice
They died fast under an underwater volcanic flow
They were sealed inside drops of tree resin
They dried out slowly on a hot desert shore

items.explain: The extraordinary preservation was probably due to their rapid death after an underwater pyroclastic flow.

items.prompt: Trilobites survived for hundreds of millions of years. Which best describes how they finally disappeared?

options.label: Wiped out suddenly alongside the dinosaurs
Died out soon after first appearing
Lost in a single Devonian catastrophe
A long decline, then a Permian end

items.explain: After peaking in the Cambrian and Ordovician, they declined through the Devonian and the last few vanished in the end-Permian mass extinction.

items.prompt: Roughly how long were the largest trilobites?

options.label: About 2 cm
More than 70 cm
About 10 cm
About 30 cm

items.explain: The largest trilobites were more than 70 centimetres long and may have weighed up to 4.5 kilograms.

items.prompt: Some trilobites evolved smooth bodies that lost most of their surface detail. What is this thought to signal?

options.label: That they had reached a very old age
That they lived in very cold water
A burrowing or open-water way of life
That their fossils were badly worn down

items.explain: This trend, called effacement, is believed to indicate either a burrowing lifestyle or a pelagic, open-water one.
